harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured and verified the three-node OpenTelemetry routing gateway with HTTPS, mutual TLS, strict namespace rejection, persistent JSON storage, and no cross-routing or duplicate delivery.
actions_performed: Installed checksum-verified OpenTelemetry Collector Contrib 0.159.0 on all nodes and enabled hardened systemd services.
Created CA-signed gateway, collector, and client certificates; client credentials are protected under /root/otel-client on node1.
Configured move-based payments and inventory routes with retries and queues disabled.
Configured namespace filters and append-mode JSON exporters on node2 and node3.
Executed authenticated, unauthenticated, valid, missing-namespace, and unsupported-namespace probes.

evidence.requirement: OTLP/HTTP over HTTPS on node1:4318 with client credentials
evidence.summary: Final configuration validates, port 4318 is listening, credentials exist under /root/otel-client, a certificate-less request failed TLS, and authenticated requests returned HTTP 200.
End-to-end exports succeeded using the gateway client identity; both backend collectors rejected TLS handshakes without a client certificate.

evidence.requirement: Route payments only to node2 and inventory only to node3 without duplicates
evidence.summary: Files began empty. After one trace per namespace, each destination contained exactly one valid JSON record and its expected marker once, with zero cross-route markers.

evidence.requirement: Reject missing or unsupported service.namespace values
evidence.summary: Missing and unsupported namespaces both returned HTTP 503, while both backend files remained unchanged and contained zero rejected markers.

evidence.requirement: Retain accepted traces at the required paths
evidence.summary: node2 retains payments traces at /var/lib/otel/payments.json and node3 retains inventory traces at /var/lib/otel/inventory.json; both exporters use append mode, configurations validate, and services remain active and enabled.
